what: The Online Timer is a countdown timer that runs in your browser. You set hours, minutes and seconds, or tap a preset, and it counts down to zero. When the time is up, it shows a message, changes the browser tab title and can play a beeping sound.
It is useful for cooking, studying in focused blocks, workouts and rest periods, short meetings, exams, games and breaks. It works on computers, tablets and phones with nothing to install.
The timer runs on your own device. No account is needed and nothing is sent to a server.
uses: Set the exact minutes for pasta, eggs or baking and hear a beep when it is done.
Use the “25 min” preset for a focused study block, then a “5 min” break.
Time a plank, a rest between sets or a full training round.
Keep a presentation or a stand-up meeting to a fixed length.
Show a large countdown on a projector so everyone can see the time left.
tutorial: Type numbers in “Hours”, “Minutes” and “Seconds”. The big display above shows the time you set. Hours go up to 99, minutes and seconds up to 59.
Click “1 min”, “5 min”, “10 min”, “25 min” or “1 hour” to fill the boxes at once. A preset also stops and resets any running timer.
“Play a sound when time is up” is ticked by default. Untick it for a silent timer that only shows a message.
Click “Start”. The display counts down and the browser tab title shows the time left, so you can see it from another tab.
Click “Pause” to stop the countdown. The button changes to “Resume”. Click it to continue from the same point.
The display shows 00:00, the message says “Time is up!”, the tab title changes to “Time is up!”, and three short beeps play if the sound option is ticked.
Click “Reset” to stop the timer and go back to the time in the boxes, ready to start again.
features: Set any time from 1 second up to 99 hours, 59 minutes and 59 seconds.
One click sets 1, 5, 10 or 25 minutes, or 1 hour.
Three short beeps play at the end. You can turn this off with the checkbox.
The tab title shows the remaining time, so you can work in another tab and still see it.
Stop the countdown and continue later without losing time.
The timer uses the real clock, so it stays correct even if the browser slows the page in a background tab.

example.title: Worked example: a 25-minute study session
example.text: Click the “25 min” preset. The boxes change to 0 hours, 25 minutes and 0 seconds, and the display shows 25:00. Click “Start”. One second later the display and the tab title show 24:59. After 10 minutes you click “Pause” at 15:00, and later click “Resume”, and it continues from 15:00. When it reaches zero, the message “Time is up!” appears and you hear three beeps. Click “5 min” for your break, and then “Start” again.

tips: Keep the page open. Closing the tab or the browser stops the timer.
Hours are only shown in the display when the time is one hour or more, for example 01:30:00.
On phones, keep the screen on. A locked phone may pause sounds from web pages.
Click “Start” once before you walk away. The sound is unlocked by your click, which many browsers require.
Use the presets as a quick start, then change the boxes if you need a time like 7 minutes 30 seconds.
problems: All three boxes are 0 or empty. Enter a time or click a preset.
The timer stopped when I closed or reloaded the tab
The timer lives in the page. Closing or reloading it clears the countdown. Keep the tab open until the time is up.
Changing the hours, minutes or seconds boxes while paused, or clicking “Reset” or a preset, starts again from the boxes. Click “Resume” without editing the boxes to continue.
I typed 75 minutes but it shows 59
Minutes and seconds are limited to 59. Enter 1 hour and 15 minutes instead.
